chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Hammad ibn 'Uthman said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the musk of the Ka'bah and the musk of the grave that remains in the garment of Ihram, so he said, 'There is no harm with it; they are both purifying.' And whenever perfume settles on a person's garment, there is no harm in removing it with his hand and washing it. Narrated.

key_terms.ثَوْبِ اَلْإِحْرَامِ: The garment of Ihram (sacred state for pilgrimage)
key_terms.خَلُوق: Musk or perfume, specifically referring to the scent from the Ka'bah or graves

ai.seo_question: Does remaining perfume from the Ka'bah invalidate the Ihram of a pilgrim?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the presence of musk from the Ka'bah or graves on a pilgrim's garment does not invalidate Ihram, as these scents are considered 'purifying' (tahur). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between the scent of a substance and the substance itself, allowing the pilgrim to remove the scent by hand or washing without incurring a penalty, thereby facilitating the practical observance of pilgrimage rites.
